title: Relative Clauses: who, which, where, that
grammarTitle: Relative Clauses — Defining with who, which, where, that
grammarNote: Относительные придаточные предложения (relative clauses) используются для определения или уточнения, о ком или о чём идёт речь. Они отвечают на вопросы "который?", "которая?", "где?". В определительных придаточных (defining relative clauses) без запятых: WHO — для людей, WHICH — для вещей/предметов, WHERE — для мест, THAT — может заменять who или which.

grammarTable.subject: who
grammarTable.example: "She's a person WHO reads everything carefully." / "The man WHO taught me."

grammarTable.subject: which
grammarTable.example: "A book WHICH changed my thinking." / "The café WHICH serves Kazakh food."

grammarTable.subject: where
grammarTable.example: "A room WHERE nothing decorative exists." / "The library WHERE I studied."

grammarTable.subject: that
grammarTable.example: "A place THAT inspires me." / "The people THAT run it." (less formal than who)

grammarTable.subject: whose
grammarTable.example: "A student WHOSE notes I read." / "A café WHOSE menu hasn't changed."

grammarTable.subject: when
grammarTable.example: "I remember the day WHEN I first arrived." / "A time WHEN things were simpler."

grammarExtra.title: who, which, where — choosing the right pronoun

rows.example: "She's the professor WHO taught me linguistics." / "The students WHO arrived early."
"A book WHICH I found in the library." / "The soup WHICH my grandmother always ordered."
"A city WHERE everyone knows your name." / "The bench WHERE she sits every morning."
"The café THAT my grandmother used to visit." / "The woman THAT taught me." (less formal).
"The book that changed my life." (which book? → the one that changed my life — essential info)
"The library, which was built in the Soviet era, is beautiful." (extra info, not essential)
"The library, WHICH was built in 1960, is beautiful." (non-defining = must use "which", not "that")
"A woman WHOSE notes I found." = her notes / "A café WHOSE menu hasn't changed." = its menu.
"The year WHEN I arrived." = the year; at that time.
"She is a student. Her essay won." → "She is a student WHOSE essay won." ✅
"The moment WHEN everything changed." / "A time WHEN life was simpler."
✅ "The place WHERE I was born." — places use "where" not "which" when no preposition follows.
✅ "The man WHO teaches me." — people always use "who" (or "that" informally).
✅ "The book WHICH/THAT she wrote." — things use "which" or "that", never "who".

rows.form: ✗ "This is the professor that whose notes I found."
rows.example: ✅ Use WHOSE for possession: "The professor WHOSE notes I found." ✅

grammarTip:
Относительные местоимения — простая схема:
→ ЧЕЛОВЕК: WHO (или that в разговорной речи)
→ ВЕЩЬ: WHICH (или that)
→ МЕСТО: WHERE
→ ВЛАДЕНИЕ: WHOSE (чей)
→ ВРЕМЯ: WHEN

Определительные (без запятых) = essential information
"A place THAT inspires me."

Неопределительные (с запятыми) = extra information
"The library, WHICH was built in 1960, is beautiful."
→ В неопределительных НЕЛЬЗЯ использовать THAT!

💡 Тест: уберите придаточное.
Если смысл сохранился → неопределительное (нужны запятые).
Если смысл изменился → определительное (без запятых).

exercises.text: She's a person ___ always pays attention to what she reads.
exercises.hint: A PERSON → use "who". "She's a person WHO always pays attention." ✅

exercises.text: It's a book ___ changed my whole approach to reading.
exercises.hint: A BOOK (thing) → use "which" or "that". "A book WHICH changed my approach." ✅

exercises.text: It's a city ___ everyone knows your name.
exercises.hint: A CITY (place) → use "where". "A city WHERE everyone knows your name." ✅

exercises.text: She's a librarian ___ notes I found in every book I read.
exercises.hint: "WHOSE notes" = possession (HER notes). "A librarian WHOSE notes I found." ✅

exercises.text: "The people who run the café." — Can you say "the people that run"?
opts: Yes — "that" can replace "who" in defining clauses (informal)
Yes — but only in formal writing
exercises.correct: Yes — "that" can replace "who" in defining clauses (informal)
exercises.hint: "that" can replace "who" in informal, defining relative clauses. "The people THAT run the café." ✅ (informal)

exercises.text: I remember the day ___ I first arrived in Uralsk.
exercises.hint: "WHEN" for time (the day, the moment, the year). "The day WHEN I arrived." ✅

exercises.instruction: Is "that" possible in this non-defining clause?
exercises.text: "The library, ___ was built in the Soviet era, is beautiful."
exercises.hint: Non-defining clause (with commas) → NEVER use "that". Must use "which". "The library, WHICH was built in the Soviet era..." ✅

exercises.text: The bench ___ she sits every morning faces the morning sun.
exercises.hint: A BENCH (place where she sits) → use "where". "The bench WHERE she sits." ✅

exercises.text: She's a student ___ notebook is filled with interesting questions.
exercises.hint: "WHOSE notebook" = the notebook belongs to her. "A student WHOSE notebook is filled with questions." ✅

exercises.instruction: Which sentence has the correct relative pronoun?
opts: "The book which she wrote is interesting."
"The man which taught me is here."
exercises.correct: "The book which she wrote is interesting."
exercises.hint: Book = thing → "which." ✅ "Man which" ✗ (should be "who"), "place who" ✗ (should be "where"), "feeling which" ✓ but less natural.

exercises.instruction: Which is a defining relative clause (no commas)?
opts: "Kamila, who studies linguistics, is from Almaty."
"The café that my grandmother used to visit."
"The library, which is in Almaty, is beautiful."
"Amir, who studies computer science, is from Aktobe."
exercises.correct: "The café that my grandmother used to visit."
exercises.hint: Defining = no commas; essential information. "The café THAT my grandmother used to visit." ✅ (tells us WHICH café)

exercises.text: "There's a reading room ___ she used to study for exams."
exercises.hint: A ROOM (place) → "where". "A reading room WHERE she used to study for exams." ✅

questions.text: "She's a person ___ reads everything." Choose the pronoun.
questions.hint: "who" = people. "She's a person WHO reads everything." ✅

questions.text: "A book ___ changed my life." Choose the pronoun.
questions.hint: "which" = things. "A book WHICH changed my life." ✅ (or "that")

questions.text: "A place ___ you feel at home." Choose the pronoun.
questions.hint: "where" = places. "A place WHERE you feel at home." ✅
"WHOSE" = possession. "A librarian WHOSE notes I found." ✅ (the notes belong to her)
"that" replaces "who" or "which" only in DEFINING (no comma) clauses. Not in non-defining (comma) clauses! ✅

questions.text: "The library, ___ was built in 1960, is beautiful." (extra info)
questions.hint: Non-defining (commas) → must use "WHICH", never "that". "The library, WHICH was built in 1960..." ✅

questions.text: "The man which taught me." — What is wrong?
opts: "which" should be "who" — man is a person
questions.correct: "which" should be "who" — man is a person
questions.hint: ✅ "The man WHO taught me." — "which" is for things. People always use "who". ✅

questions.text: "A café whose menu hasn't changed." — "whose" refers to:
questions.hint: "WHOSE menu" = the café's menu. "Whose" shows possession. ✅

questions.text: A defining relative clause is one that:
opts: Defines/identifies which person or thing you mean
questions.correct: Defines/identifies which person or thing you mean
questions.hint: Defining = essential. "The book THAT changed my life." — tells you WHICH book. Without it, the sentence loses meaning.

questions.text: "The students who study hard succeed." — Can you replace "who" with "that"?
questions.hint: "The students THAT study hard succeed." ✅ — informal. "that" replaces "who" in defining clauses.

questions.text: "It's the room ___ she does all her thinking."
questions.hint: "where" for places. "The room WHERE she does all her thinking." ✅

questions.text: "She is a student ___ work I always admire." Choose the pronoun.
questions.hint: "WHOSE work I admire" = possession (her work). "A student WHOSE work I always admire." ✅
"A place WHERE she grew up." ✅ — place → where. ✓ Others: "book who" ✗, "man which" ✗, "café where serves" ✗.

questions.text: "There was a time ___ we didn't have smartphones."
questions.hint: "when" after time expressions (year, day, moment, time). "A time WHEN we didn't have smartphones." ✅

questions.text: The non-defining relative clause uses commas because:
opts: The information is extra — the sentence is complete without it
questions.correct: The information is extra — the sentence is complete without it
questions.hint: Non-defining = extra info in commas. Remove it and the sentence still makes sense and identifies the noun.
